Done — passed on the first execution.

**Plan** (`out/T3/plan.yaml`, 40 non-comment lines): one `cast_` transform wrapped in preflight and post-edit asserts.

The whole edit is a single in-place cast targeting an anchored regex:

```
model\.layers\.\d+\.(?:self_attn\.[qkvo]_proj|mlp\.(?:gate|up|down)_proj)\.weight
```

`cast_` rather than `cast` because names must not change and in-place preserves state-dict order, which the shard packer walks. No `delete` — this checkpoint has no buffers.

The required check "exactly 112 tensors are bfloat16" isn't one assert, since `dtype` only constrains what its reference matches. It's pinned down by three: the projection pattern matches exactly 112 and all are bfloat16; the complement (same regex behind a negative lookahead, `(?!...\.weight$).*`) is all float32; and the total is still 114. Plus the named spot checks on `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight`, `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight`.

Sharding is `shard: 256MB` — binary units, so exactly the 268,435,456-byte budget.

**Verification** of `out/T3/` against the input:

| | |
|---|---|
| tensors | 114, names identical to input |
| dtypes | 112 bfloat16, 2 float32 (`embed_tokens`, `lm_head`) |
| values | bit-exact for all 114 — projections equal `i.to(torch.bfloat16)`, the rest unchanged |
| shards | 10; the two 412 MB float32 tensors alone in shards 1–2, the rest packed at exactly 268,435,456 bytes |
| index | `weight_map` covers all 114 and matches what each file actually holds; `total_size` correct |

Report written to `out/T3/REPORT.md`. Two things I flagged there as unclear in the task text: the objective mentions norms/biases/buffers that this checkpoint doesn't have, and the `dtype` assert's docs don't say whether a multi-match reference requires every match to hold (unlike `reads`/`writes`, which say so explicitly) — I relied on the every-match reading and cross-checked with `count`.
